lines.text: Plate three. The oil lamp, in Latin, lucerna.
At the back, a small ring, just wide enough for one finger, to carry the light from room to room.
In the middle of the shallow dish, a little hole, where olive oil was poured in, slowly, so it would not spill.
And at the narrow end, a twist of linen drew up the oil, and held one small, steady flame.
Made by the thousand in clay moulds, lamps like this kept the long Roman nights soft, and warm, and quiet.
